subject: MedSys pilot: geo-tether request and routing shield plan
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@medsys.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsys.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot request: geo-tether + routing shield for PHI flows

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have sign-off internally to run a 6‑week pilot for our clinical notes ingestion pipeline, but two compliance boxes are must-haves before we start:

- All EU traffic must remain tethered to our EU-dedicated footprint (data residency requirement).
- Fallbacks to public/shared hosted variants cannot be used for this pilot; if a node is unavailable the request should fail rather than fall back to a hosted variant.
- We also need to pin to a specific private model variant for parity with our validation work (we've validated "rwd-priv-t5q" at 8-bit quant).

I've attached the specific security questionnaire items that triggered this ask. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can implement a short-lived policy for the pilot that: geo-tethers requests to EU-only, disables automatic fallback to public-hosted models, and forces the selected model variant?

Happy to hop on a call — procurement is looped for contract language once we confirm feasibility.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Integrations, MedSys Health

Attachment: medsys-security-questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 246 KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@medsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: geo-tether + routing shield for PHI flows

Elena — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Short answer: we can do this, but there are operational trade-offs we need to align on.

Quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
- Is the requirement that *all* tokens for any request must be processed on EU-dedicated instances, or only inference execution (i.e., are any pre/post-processing steps allowed outside EU)?
- For the fail behavior, do you prefer explicit 503 with a human-readable error (preferred by security) or an automated retry into a cold private pool we reserve for this pilot?

Karthik — can you sketch the product/ops work? Marissa / Ben: I included you to keep commercial and rollout timing aware. I'll propose a short working session tomorrow to align the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@medsys.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: geo-tether + routing shield for PHI flows

Stephanie / team — technical notes and proposed approach below. I'm putting this on paper to capture constraints and the least-risk implementation.

Background constraints:
- Our standard smart-routing will fallback to compatible hosted variants if dedicated capacity is exhausted. For this pilot that behavior must be suppressed.
- A strict geo-tether requires that both inference and KV cache access occur in the EU region (we can do the control-plane decision anywhere).

Proposed implementation (pilot scope):
1) Create a transient routing policy "eu-shield-pilot-2027" that enforces:
   - region_tag == eu AND customer_tag == medsys
   - allowed_model_list == ["rwd-priv-t5q"] (force variant)
   - fallback_policy == "disable_public_fallback" (requests will fail with 503 + structured error if no dedicated capacity)
2) Reserve a small private pool (2x A100 equivalent) for the pilot window and set autoscale to manual burst only; ops will monitor and manually add capacity if saturation occurs.
3) KV/prefix cache: populate a regional cache and pin to the same EU pool to avoid cross-region calls.
4) Telemetry/alerts: trace ID tagging to ensure any request that would cross-region is rejected and logged; export to MedSys S3 bucket for audit.

Operational notes:
- This approach requires a short runbook for on-call ops to follow when the reserved pool is saturated. I attached a draft runbook for review.
- We will need a short legal/contract carveout around retries and SLOs since fallback is intentionally disabled.

I'll be available to run a dry-run in our staging EU cluster Friday.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Serving
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rwd-eu-shield-runbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@medsys.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: geo-tether + routing shield for PHI flows

Elena / team — great to see progress. A few commercial items so procurement has clarity: 
- We'll confirm the reserved pool pricing (flat monthly + overage per token) and add a short SLA carveout that specifies the system will return a deterministic rejection when capacity is unavailable.
- Legal will draft a Mutual Pilot Agreement (MPA) that includes exception language for fallback suppression and audit expectations.
- For DocuSign: can procurement confirm the signer and whether we should route through their legal inbox or an integration specialist?

Marissa / Stephanie — can you take lead on the MPA and pricing note? I'll coordinate the quick quote.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@medsys.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: geo-tether + routing shield for PHI flows — action plan

Team — summarizing next steps and owners so we can close the loop with MedSys: 

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Finalize transient routing policy and create "eu-shield-pilot-2027" (Karthik) / ETA: 2027-12-07 EOD
- Provision reserved EU pool and enable manual burst (Infra Ops — coordinated by Karthik) / ETA: 2027-12-08
- Draft MPA and pricing note with explicit fallback suppression clause (Marissa / Ben) / ETA: 2027-12-06
- Security evidence bundle + audit export path to MedSys S3 (Security & Integrations — Stephanie) / ETA: 2027-12-06
- Runbook review & staging dry-run (Karthik + Ops) / Dry-run: 2027-12-10
- Schedule kickoff call with MedSys (Stephanie) — proposed: 2027-12-09 10:00 CET (I sent a calendar hold)

Elena — if that timeline looks aligned we will start the MPA and setup work immediately. I've attached the two artifacts we referenced (runbook + MPA draft).

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. If we see continued interest we can explore automating a permanent "shield" policy product in H2 2028, but for now we will treat this as a pilot with explicit manual controls.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rwd-eu-shield-runbook-v1.pdf, medsys-mpa-draft.docx
